slots.body:

slots.title: U.S. close — Nov. 13, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 finished at 7,592.40, down 0.4% (-26.98 points), with an intraday range of 7,550.84 to 7,652.76.
The session was part of a broader tech-led narrative tied to sudden leadership change at the center of the AI trade, with large-cap indexes moving in lockstep rather than diverging.

The Nasdaq Composite closed at 25,366.09, also -0.4%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average ended at 52,297.09, -0.4%.
Despite the uniform percentage move among those three, the Russell 2000 was weaker at 2,799.06, -1.7%, suggesting more pressure under the surface in smaller companies than in the headline indexes.

NVIDIA was the standout megacap decliner among the most watched names, closing at 166.19, -4.3%.
Coverage linked the drop to fallout from the abrupt exit of a key figure behind the AI boom, with technology stocks absorbing the shock.
Trading interest showed up in the actives list, where $NVDA sat alongside levered chip products.

Rotation within semiconductors showed up in the price data: Advanced Micro Devices rose 5.9% to 585.30 and Broadcom gained 5.5% to 364.36 on heavy volume (AMD volume 55,014,886; AVGO 43,502,367).
Taiwan Semiconductor slipped 1.9% to 405.49.
Oracle, which had been a recent mover, eased 1.0% to 127.14.

Among other megacaps, Alphabet Class A shares rose 1.8% to 298.70 and Microsoft edged up 0.4% to 523.00.
Meta fell 0.8% to 623.61, Netflix declined 2.9% to 62.69, and Visa lost 1.2% to 420.31.
Apple was essentially flat, -0.1% at 354.88.
Exxon Mobil rose 1.8% to 169.78; Johnson & Johnson gained 1.1% to 283.52; Costco touched a session high of 1,102.84 and closed 0.4% higher at 1,092.21.

The CBOE Volatility Index closed at 18.70, up 6.9% from 17.49, with an intraday high of 19.34.
That move accompanied the equity slip rather than a calm, range-bound tape.

In cross-assets, gold futures rose 0.7% to 3,914.10.
The United States Oil Fund (a common WTI exposure) gained 3.3% to 146.07, while Brent crude was -0.3% at 95.57.
The dollar proxy (UUP) ticked up 0.2% to 29.42.
Bitcoin fell 4.1% to 68,476.28.

Treasury yields in the dataset carried a November 10 stamp: the 2-year at 4.7%, 10-year at 5.0%, and the 2s10s spread at 0.25 percentage points.
Fresh yield prints were not part of this close bundle.

Overseas indexes in the feed were mixed: Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 0.8% to 61,299.33, the FTSE 100 gained 0.3% to 10,863.09, the Hang Seng fell 1.1% to 23,744.50, and the Germany ETF proxy (EWG) was -0.5% at 42.81.

The economic calendar listed multiple U.S. producer-price (PPI) releases for October at 13:30 on this date, including month-over-month headline PPI with a 0.4% estimate and core month-over-month at 0.3%.
No actual PPI figures were included in this data snapshot, so the recap stops at what was scheduled.

No earnings results with reported actuals appeared in the earnings calendar for this bundle.
Sector performance breakdowns were not populated in the feed for this session.
